$comment: Illustrative machine-readable CBOM profile for procurement. DERIVED: extends the interface disclosure baseline v0.10 (draft) and adds no per-interface attribute. It selects and tightens, which places it in the disclosure group (draft decision 0023): a document rich enough for the baseline, and with the implementing library stated, answers it without being reissued.
title: Procurement and Tender Conformance (Example)

objective.$comment: C1. The consumer is the buyer, not the operator the product will later serve. The decision is about the tender response, and every rule below traces to a reason a buyer would send a response back.
objective.consumer: A buyer evaluating tender responses for a product it will operate but did not build and cannot inspect.
objective.decision: Whether a supplier's cryptographic disclosure is complete and specific enough to compare with other responses and to hold the supplier to over the contract, or whether it must be clarified or rejected.
decisionOptions: accept the disclosure for evaluation alongside other responses
return it for clarification, naming the failing rules
reject the response as non-compliant with the tender's disclosure requirement

scope.$comment: C11. Narrows the base to a product as offered: subject type 'product', stage 'implemented'. A tender response describes the product being offered; a statement of what it is meant to do is a promise, and belongs in the commercial response where its status is understood.

appliesTo.$comment: Carrier acceptance. The target is CycloneDX 2.0, pinned to CycloneDX/specification 2.0-dev commit 76f185c (23 October 2026) until Ecma ratifies the release; the pinned schema is in tests/schemas/cyclonedx-2.0. 'min' is the oldest version the adapter reads: CycloneDX 1.6 and 1.7 documents are evaluated and flagged legacy, because the tools that produce CBOMs today emit 1.x. Below 'min', evaluation is refused. A derived profile may narrow this range and may not widen it.

overrides.note: Tightened by removing withholdability, as the migration profile does. A buyer holds the product for the life of the contract and must be able to match every interface to library advisories during it. A tender response is made under the tender's confidentiality terms, which is where a supplier's reason to withhold the library is answered.

productRules.description: Product declares at least one storage interface for key material at rest, or states why it has none
productRules.note: The structural rule a buyer most needs after the baseline's P2. Responses describe the interfaces traffic crosses and are silent about where keys are kept. A product that keeps no keys, or keeps them in a hardware module outside the product, satisfies the rule by saying so, the same way the baseline's P2 treats a product with no management surface.

productRules.description: Product states coverage of all interfaces, or of all externally reachable ones
productRules.note: interface-disclosure#P4 requires coverage to be stated. A partial disclosure cannot be compared across responses, because a missing interface could be absent or merely unlisted, so a buyer returns it. Stated as a new rule on the same attribute rather than as an override of interface-disclosure#P4, with its own narrower vocabulary.

exclusions.item: Scoring, ranking or weighting of responses
exclusions.reason: A judgement, and the buyer's own. The profile decides whether a disclosure can be evaluated, not how it scores. See decision 0002.
Asked for by a change-planning profile. A buyer who needs them names the PQC migration profile in the tender as well, and the supplier answers both with one richer document.

exclusions.item: Algorithm requirements such as a minimum key size or an approved list
exclusions.reason: Policy applied to the disclosed facts, not a fact about the disclosure. A buyer evaluates them with its own versioned policy over a conforming document.

artifacts.$comment: C9. One rich document serves several consumers: the product record written for migration planning is read unchanged against this profile.

changelog.summary: Initial draft. Extends the interface disclosure baseline v0.8: narrows accepted lifecycle stages, tightens I9 by removing withholdability, and adds product rules P5 (storage interface or stated absence) and P6 (coverage at least all-external).

changes.summary: First published, pinned to the Interface Disclosure Baseline v0.9 and scoped to products at 'implemented'.

Renumbered the profile's own product rules from P5 and P6 to P1 and P2, so that numbering starts at 1 in every profile. The rules are unchanged. Citations of procurement#P5 and procurement#P6 now read procurement#P1 and procurement#P2.

changelog.summary: Attribute names made clearer and consistent across the profiles (drafts/attribute-naming-review.md; decision 0028). The version is unchanged because no release has been published.

changes.summary: Renamed: storageInterfaceAbsence → absent:storage-interface. A record that uses the previous name no longer conforms.
